title: RSF Renews Assault on Al-Murrah Villages Under Communications Blackout, North Kordofan
detail: RSF forces renewed their ground assault on al-Murrah villages west of Barah town, North Kordofan, on May 30, 2026 — the day after their Eid al-Adha massacre that killed at least 27 civilians. A complete communications blackout was imposed across the area, severely limiting the flow of information to humanitarian monitors and journalists. The renewed assault follows a documented RSF pattern of multi-day attacks on civilian villages in North Kordofan: suppressing survivor testimony, completing looting and property destruction, and preventing civilian flight toward SAF-held lines. Al-Murrah lies in the contested western arc of North Kordofan, adjacent to RSF positions anchored at RSF-recaptured Bara (March 2026). SAF's Kordofan counteroffensive axes — particularly toward Dilling, Dibebad, and the Darfur–Kordofan supply corridor — make the broader Bara–Al-Murrah axis a key RSF defensive and atrocity zone. Communications blackouts have preceded and accompanied RSF atrocities at El Fasher, Wad Madani, and multiple Darfur towns throughout the war.

media.caption: RSF renewed ground assault on al-Murrah villages west of Barah, North Kordofan on May 30 — a complete communications blackout prevented independent casualty verification of the follow-on attack.

title: RSF Drone Strike Kills 10 on Abu Zabad–Al-Fula Road, West Kordofan
detail: An RSF drone struck vehicles traveling along the Abu Zabad–Al-Fula road in West Kordofan State on May 30, 2026, killing at least 10 people. The strike targeted civilian vehicles on a major road connecting Abu Zabad town to the West Kordofan state capital Al-Fula (El Fula). West Kordofan has faced intensifying RSF drone attacks throughout May 2026 — including a devastating SAF retaliatory strike on the Ghubaysh market (May 19, 28 killed) — as RSF seeks to maintain pressure on SAF-aligned population centers even as SAF makes ground gains in North Kordofan and Blue Nile. IOM documented approximately 46,000 newly displaced people in West Kordofan during May 2026 alone, driven by the combination of RSF drone strikes and ground combat. The Abu Zabad–Al-Fula road is a strategic route used by civilians and potentially for SAF military logistics; targeting it is consistent with RSF's broader strategy of interdicting SAF supply lines in the Kordofan theater while inflicting civilian casualties to generate population displacement. The strike follows the established RSF pattern of using drone-loitering munitions to attack vehicles and road convoys across Sudan's Kordofan states, documented in OHCHR's May 2026 high-alert statement on drone warfare.

title: Pattern of RSF Drone Attacks on El-Obeid Continues — 10–24 Killed on May 29 Including 8 Children
detail: Reporting from May 29–30, 2026 confirmed continued RSF drone strikes on El-Obeid (Al-Ubayyid), the SAF-held capital of North Kordofan State. A drone strike on a residential house on May 29 killed between 10 and 24 civilians, including 8 children, according to multiple sources. The Sudan Doctors Network — which has tracked drone casualties throughout 2026 — reported 13 killed (including 8 children) from the residential strike. PBS NewsHour cited 24 killed including children, while Dabanga reported 10 killed. Discrepancies likely reflect different strike events or varying counts from the same incident. El-Obeid has faced near-daily RSF drone attacks since the SAF broke the ground siege in February 2025; OHCHR documented at least 880 civilian drone deaths across Sudan in January–April 2026 with drones responsible for over 80% of conflict-related civilian deaths. The continued strikes represent RSF's strategy of maintaining pressure on SAF-controlled North Kordofan even after losing the ground siege, using its loitering munition capabilities developed with UAE and Libyan supply chain support.
